# quick :: rv_soyoil_palm

**Q:** Palm oil's supply picture has been shifting. How does that reach soybean oil, and where does the balance between the two sheets stand this marketing year?

**TL;DR.** Palm reaches soybean oil through substitution: when palm gets dear or scarce, price-sensitive food and fuel buyers move onto soyoil, and when palm is cheap and stock-rich they move the other way. As of 2026-09-16 the two sheets do NOT lean the same way  --  Malaysian palm stocks have risen in each of the last 4 months [N84] to 2.62832 MMT [N81], which loosens palm, while the US soybean-oil stocks-to-use ratio sits at 5.67 % [N41], the 1st percentile of its own record [N43], which points toward higher soyoil prices; the tighter leg is soybean oil, and I expect it to dominate the pair.

**Why.** ## Mechanism

**The substitution channel.** Palm and soyoil are the two interchangeable oils in the same food and biodiesel pool. The driver model carries the palm-soyoil premium at high confidence on BOTH boards: a wide soyoil premium pushes buyers into palm (supportive of palm, pressuring soyoil), a narrow one pulls demand back to soyoil. That is the whole transmission  --  it is a relative-price gate, not a volume story.

**Where each sheet sits.** On palm, rising month-end Malaysian inventories are the model's high-confidence loosening driver, and that is what the record shows now. On soyoil, a falling stocks-to-use ratio is the high-confidence tightening driver, and it is at the bottom of its own record. Those two do not cancel  --  they compound in the SAME direction for the pair: palm loosening while soyoil tightens widens soyoil's premium and pushes marginal demand toward palm, which is the mechanism that eventually caps soyoil and cushions palm.

**Where it turns convex.** On the soyoil side the thin stocks buffer is the convexity: with the ratio in its lowest percentile, any further demand pull (a firm crush, a fast export week) has little cushion to absorb it, so the upside response is right-tailed rather than linear. Against that, the loose palm sheet is the natural brake  --  cheap, well-stocked palm is the substitute that rations soyoil demand, so the skew is asymmetric, not one-way. On palm itself the loosening is roughly linear: stocks are building, not collapsing.

**What is NOT firing.** The price-supportive palm supply squeeze needs three of its six drivers; only two of the loudest readings here belong to it (El Nino and the palm-belt drought reading), below its own threshold. Note the drought, export-levy, domestic-obligation and export-ban readings on palm are phases of ONE Indonesian series, so they are one source of risk, not four.

## The record

Palm, read through 2026-07-01: production 1,792,979 MT [N1], exports 1,392,178 MT [N3], closing stocks 2,628,325 MT [N2] and a stocks-to-use ratio of 1.88792 [N4]; stocks rose +0.0845 MMT on the month [N83] and in each of the last 4 months [N84]. Soybean oil, read through 2026: stocks-to-use 5.67 % [N41], -1.2 sigma [N42], falling in each of the last two marketing years, past the desk's own very-tight line. Argentine export tax sits one hop upstream at 6.65 MMT [N44], 97th percentile [N46]  --  the model's high-confidence channel by which restricted Argentine soyoil exports support world soyoil; its stated effect window closed 2026-06-30. The CBOT board crush reads 2.6 USD/bu [N65], 92nd percentile [N67], read through 2026-08-21  --  oil-led crush pull, on the model's medium-confidence edge. US soyoil export pace reads 1.81 thousand MT [N59], 28th percentile [N61], behind the desk's line, and weekly exports changed -0.317 thousand MT week-on-week [N82]  --  the one leg that loosens soyoil. Managed money held 99823 contracts [N35], 88th percentile [N37]; the model carries positioning as amplification, not cause.

On the price layer, palm reads 1,117 USD/mt and soyoil 1,638 USD/mt (World Bank, August 2026) [N11][N12], with palm 0.269096 sigma [N13] and soyoil 1.21357 sigma [N14] against their own five-year means  --  soyoil is the leg sitting far higher in its own record; the gap itself is not a served series. USDA's world palm and world soyoil balance sheets for this marketing year carry NO figure at this as-of, so the world-basis comparison cannot be made; the national production records that do exist are 20,200,000 MT for palm [N23] and 21,800,000 MT for soybean oil [N24], each on its own scope.

On substitution as documented: in MY 2022/23 consumers shifted to palm from soyoil as palm fell to roughly 25 percent cheaper than soybean oil [E2], the same gate running the other way; a USDA balance-sheet note from 1998 put it plainly, that increased palm supply prospects weigh on soyoil prices [E3]. Both are dated history, not current reads.

**The 2020-08 to 2021-01 episode.** Over that window the palm-canola substitution relation held: ICE canola settled +27.78 % on its January 2021 delivery [N86], with the Canadian-dollar rate moving -4.7833 % against the US dollar in the same window [N87]  --  each figure a move inside its own currency, US dollars and Canadian dollars, no rate applied. The palm-Zhengzhou rapeseed oil relation held too: rapeseed oil +17.6352 % on its January 2021 delivery [N88], with the yuan rate -6.2184 % [N89], again each in its own currency. The palm-soyoil relation held: CBOT soybean oil +40.1812 % on its January 2021 delivery [N90]. The palm-soybean relation held: CBOT soybeans +49.5877 % [N91]. Palm itself settled +38.9844 % on its February 2021 delivery [N85]. All in-sample on that named window only. For the MATIF rapeseed leg the window predates that board's own price history, so there is no figure. The corpus also documents report windows in 2009-10..2010-05 and 2010-09..2011-06 with no citable item  --  I will not narrate those.

**How far each layer reaches.** The numbers are read as of 2026-09-16, newest read through 20260904 and oldest 2025-12-05; the newest dated document behind this page is from 2022-03-17; the board price tape is not carried on this page. So the tape layer is the thin one here, and the documents are years older than the numbers.

## Where the record disagrees

The two sheets genuinely diverge this marketing year, and blending them would destroy the read:
- **Palm**  --  closing stocks 2.62832 MMT [N81], up in each of the last 4 months [N84], stocks-to-use 1.88792 [N4]. A loosening balance.
- **Soybean oil**  --  stocks-to-use 5.67 % [N41], 1st percentile of its own record [N43], two marketing years falling. A tightening balance.

There is also a conflict INSIDE the soyoil sheet: the tight stocks buffer and the high board crush point toward higher prices, while the export pace at the 28th percentile [N61] points the other way. Stocks-to-use is the higher-confidence driver in the model, which is why I lean to the tight side  --  that is a model ranking, not a measured attribution.

Across source tiers: the USDA balance-sheet note that palm supply weighs on soyoil [E3] and the Malaysian industry-body note that a widening palm discount hands palm the substitution share [E4] describe the same gate from opposite ends; they do not conflict on mechanism.

## What to watch

- **Soyoil stocks-to-use** [N41]  --  already past the desk's very-tight line with an unbroken two-year run lower. This is the convexity. It reads wrong if the next print turns back inside that line or the run breaks.
- **The CBOT board crush** [N65]  --  2.6 USD/bu, top decile of its own record, read through 2026-08-21; its declared zero-to-one-quarter window, counted from that reading's date, would run 2026-08-20 to 2026-11-20. Sustained high crush confirms oil-led pull; it reads wrong if the next print returns the series to the middle of its record. Note the same reading is declared in the OPPOSITE direction on CBOT soybean meal  --  the joint-product split is where crush strength resolves.
- **Malaysian month-end stocks**  --  the four-month build [N84] is the brake on soyoil's premium. A fifth build extends the divergence; a draw would start closing it.
- **Indonesian palm-belt drought** [N62]  --  the only route to a palm supply squeeze, and it sits below that pattern's own three-driver threshold today. Its stated lag is two to four quarters, so if the reading keeps rising, the effect would land well after this print.

One reach note: the ocean index reading on soybean oil [N74] is declared on thirty-four other markets  --  twenty-eight same direction, six opposite  --  so a move there is priced far beyond this pair; the nearest is ICE robusta coffee, same direction, one to four quarters, high confidence. Nothing else cleared the bar.

**Cascade / convergence**
